relations.subject: Marcel Israël Mauss
relations.evidence: The nephew of Émile Durkheim, Mauss, in his academic work, crossed the boundaries between sociology and anthropology.

relations.subject: Claude Lévi-Strauss
relations.evidence: Mauss had a significant influence upon Claude Lévi-Strauss, the founder of structural anthropology.

relations.subject: Marcel Israël Mauss
relations.evidence: He was later joined by his nephew in 1890, who was preparing for his degree in philosophy at Bordeaux.

relations.subject: Émile Durkheim
relations.evidence: In 1887, Émile Durkheim was appointed to the Université de Bordeaux.

relations.subject: Marcel Israël Mauss
relations.evidence: Between 1893 and 1894, when Mauss started to prepare for Agrégation, Durkheim, a philosophy agrégé and a member of the exam board, tutored Mauss for the exam.

relations.subject: Marcel Israël Mauss
relations.evidence: Durkheim also helped connect Mauss with Octave Hamelin, who became Mauss's close friend and an important tutor.

relations.subject: Marcel Israël Mauss
relations.evidence: In the 1890s, Mauss began his lifelong study of linguistics, Indology, Sanskrit, Hebrew, and the 'history of religions and uncivilized peoples' at the École pratique des hautes études.

relations.subject: Marcel Israël Mauss
relations.evidence: Towards the end of the century, he helped edit such left-wing papers as Le Populaire, L'Humanité and Le Mouvement socialiste, the last in collaboration with Georges Sorel.

relations.subject: Marcel Israël Mauss
relations.role: Chair of the History of Religions of Non-Civilized Peoples
relations.evidence: In 1901, Mauss was appointed to the Chair of the History of Religions of Non-Civilized Peoples at the École pratique des hautes études.

relations.subject: Marcel Israël Mauss
